title: Supply Planning & Analytics Program Manager
description:
About Blueprint

Blueprint is a technology solutions firm headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with teams across the United States. We help organizations turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes by connecting strategy and execution across AI, cloud, data, product development, and emerging technology.

Our culture is built by people who care deeply about doing exceptional work. We set high standards, take ownership, and continually challenge ourselves and one another to be better. We work hard, support each other, and take genuine pride in what we deliver for our clients, partners, and teams.

At Blueprint , you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.

Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.

About the Role
You will support network hardware demand and supply planning for a large cloud technology organization. This role focuses on evaluating weekly supply supportability, validating complex data, identifying discrepancies, and ensuring accurate reporting across the supply chain. You will collaborate with planning, sourcing, execution, and engineering stakeholders to improve reporting tools, strengthen planning processes, and provide clear insights that support business and technical decisions.
What You'll Do

• Generate weekly demand, supply, and supportability reporting for network hardware.

• Analyze week-over-week changes in demand, supply, and supportability.

• Review source data, calculations, assumptions, and system outputs to identify discrepancies or errors.

• Develop repeatable data-validation processes to maintain reporting accuracy.

• Maintain documentation and traceability for changes, assumptions, processes, and reports.

• Support weekly and monthly reporting of key performance indicators.

• Improve existing planning processes, reports, and Power BI dashboards.

• Partner with engineering teams to develop and enhance internal planning tools.

• Build dashboards that communicate supply positions, constraints, gaps, and actionable insights.

• Develop scenario-planning and “what-if” capabilities to support supply planning decisions.

• Collaborate across demand planning, supply planning, component planning, sourcing, and execution functions.

• Communicate findings, outstanding actions, and supportability updates to business and technical stakeholders.

• Track follow-up items and ensure actions are completed accurately and on time.

What You'll Bring

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in supply chain, operations, business, technology, manufacturing, sourcing, or a related field.

• 2-4 years of experience in supply planning, operations, technology-related supply chain, manufacturing, sourcing, or a related function.

• Strong supply planning experience, including demand and supply analysis.

• 2-4 years of experience using AI-enabled analytics tools to automate data validation, generate insights, and improve reporting.

• 2-4 years of advanced Excel experience.

• Working knowledge of SQL and experience developing or optimizing business intelligence tools, including Power BI.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to identify data discrepancies and implement corrective actions.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

• Effective project management and organizational skills.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to communicate with and influence both business and technical stakeholders.

• Ability to work independently, manage deadlines, and follow through on outstanding actions.

• Availability to work Pacific Time hours in a remote environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting network hardware, cloud infrastructure, or technology supply chains.

• Experience with component planning or indirect supply planning.

title: Senior Marketing Manager, ABM
description:
About Figure

Figure (NASDAQ: FIGR) is transforming capital markets through blockchain. We’re proving that blockchain isn’t just theory - it’s powering real products used by hundreds of thousands of consumers and institutions.
By combining blockchain’s transparency and efficiency with AI-driven automation, we’ve reimagined how loans are originated, funded, and traded in secondary markets. From faster processing times to lower costs and reduced bias, our technology is helping borrowers, investors, and financial institutions achieve better outcomes.
Together with our 170+ partners, we’ve originated over $22 billion in home equity loans (HELOCs) on our blockchain-native platform, making Figure the largest non-bank provider of home equity financing in the U.S. Figure ’s ecosystem also includes YLDS, an SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin that operates as a tokenized money market fund, and several other products and platforms that are reshaping consumer finance and capital markets.
We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Most Innovative Fintech Startups in 2025 and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies in Finance and Personal Finance.
About the Role
We are looking for a dynamic, driven B2B marketing professional to own our Account-Based Marketing (ABM) and cold outbound initiatives. In this role, you will act as the bridge between marketing (content, events), partnerships and sales, driving the pipeline for our key segments: Independent Mortgage Banks / Servicers, Wholesale Brokers, SMBs, Home Improvement, Banks, and Credit Unions.
You are an "outbound hacker" at heart, but one who knows how to build scalable systems, and coordinate with sales . You won't be executing every channel yourself; instead, you will bring the data together, target the accounts, define the messaging, and hand those systems off to our strong channel marketing team to deploy. Above all, you are obsessed with defining and measuring success: Sales Qualified Leads (SQLs), meetings booked, and pipeline generated.
What You’ll Do

• Build and manage the entire cold email engine. Take a hands-on approach to grading, tiering, and contact-mapping our core target segments. Identify key behavioral trigger points to launch highly impactful, "always-on" automated journeys.

• Tie everything together. You are ultimately responsible for defining what success looks like and tracking cross-channel performance to prove direct impact on meetings booked, SQLs, and pipeline generated. You will build reports in Salesforce to tell a clear story with data and diagnose CRM sync issues to convey solutions to our tech team.

• Build the targeting and messaging systems that power our ABM efforts for both cold outbounding and current prospects. Taking cold leads to warm leads to keeping the warm leads engaged throughout a longer sales cycle. Working in tandem with sales to discover key points in the sales prospecting cycle to pull accounts faster to onboarding. You will supply our highly capable channel teams with the exact data and messaging they need to execute direct mail, gifting, and LinkedIn campaigns effectively.

• While you won't be writing all the content yourself, you will act as the final filter. You should have an opinion on whether messaging will resonate and be able to give direction if the output misses the mark. You will also build streamlined systems for deploying this content to the sales team.

• Partner closely with our Field Marketing Manager to identify the highest-impact events to reach our target accounts, supplying them with the targeted ABM data and tactics (pre- and post-event) to maximize our physical presence.

What We Look For

• Proven experience in B2B marketing, specifically building Account-Based Marketing, Outbound, or Demand Generation engines.

description:
Remote Video Editor - Short-Form & Ad Creative
Remote | Argentina-Based | Full-Time Contractor | Paid in USD $5.50 - $8.50 USD/hour (approx. $950 - $1,475 USD/month full-time), paid weekly
Editor de video remoto (contrato full-time, pago en dólares) para una agencia de marketing en Estados Unidos.
Can you take raw footage and turn it into a scroll-stopping ad? Do you know why a viewer drops off at second 3 - and how to re-cut the hook so they don't? If editing is your craft and volume doesn't scare you, keep reading.
We're hiring a Video Editor on behalf of a U.S.-based marketing agency serving home service and remodeling brands. You'll produce the video creative that powers real ad campaigns - working alongside a team of media buyers and copywriters whose campaigns live or die on the quality of your edits. When your video converts, everyone sees it in the numbers.
Argentina runs just a few hours ahead of the U.S. West Coast, so you'll work a normal daytime schedule with solid overlap with the team - same-day feedback, live creative reviews, no overnight shifts.
This is a production role with real output expectations: a minimum of 30 edited pieces of content per week. If you're fast, consistent, and take pride in clean work at volume, you'll thrive here.

What You'll Do
Editing & Production

• Edit a minimum of 30 pieces of content per week - primarily short-form vertical video (ads, social clips, talking-head content, before/after project footage)

• Cut raw client footage into polished, caption-ready edits with strong hooks, tight pacing, and clean audio

• Produce multiple variations of winning ads (new hooks, new CTAs, new openers) for A/B testing

• Format deliverables correctly for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube placements

Collaboration

• Work directly with media buyers to understand which creatives are performing and iterate on winners

• Turn copywriters' scripts and hooks into finished video

• Manage your queue through the team's project management system and hit deadlines without chasing

Organization & Quality

• Maintain organized project files, brand assets, and templates for each client

• Apply client branding consistently (logos, colors, fonts, end cards)

• Self-review every edit before delivery - clean captions, no dead frames, correct aspect ratios

What We're Looking For

• 2+ years of hands-on video editing experience

• Deep proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and/or CapCut - fast enough in your tool of choice to hit 6 finished edits per day

• A portfolio of short-form edits: ads, reels, TikToks, or YouTube Shorts

• Strong instincts for hooks, pacing, and retention - you edit for the viewer who's about to scroll away

• Experience creating captions/subtitles and editing for sound-off viewing

• Professional working English (B2+) - briefs, feedback, and captions are in English; the team communicates in English daily

• Organized, deadline-driven, and consistent - volume work requires systems, not heroics

• Reliable home office setup with an editing-capable computer and stable, high-speed internet

• Availability for a consistent Monday-Friday, full-time schedule (Argentina time) with at least 4 hours of overlap with U.S. Pacific business hours

Nice to Have

• Experience using AI tools in your workflow (Runway, Descript, ElevenLabs, CapCut AI features, Midjourney, HeyGen, or similar) - we love editors who use AI to go faster without losing quality

• After Effects / motion graphics skills

• Experience editing direct-response ad creative with measurable results

• Experience editing English-language content for a U.S. audience

• Experience with home services, construction, or local business content

• Thumbnail or static creative design skills (Canva, Photoshop)

title: Director, Connectivity Partnerships
description:
About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups representing 1.8M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, one of the fastest-growing companies in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020-2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar. 

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

About the Role

Engine is looking for a Director, Connectivity Partnerships to build the partnerships and connectivity that expand what supply we can offer and how seamlessly customers can book it. The primary focus of this role is group travel - one of the largest and most underserved opportunities in business travel - where Engine is building the technology and partnerships to make booking a group as simple as booking a single room.

This role sits at the intersection of strategy, partnerships, product, and connectivity, and owns group travel end to end on the supply side. You will shape how we build across the group booking lifecycle and lead the partner discussions that bring that strategy to life with hotel chains, travel partners, and platforms across the ecosystem. Groups is a large, standalone opportunity, and this role is built for someone to own it at depth, with room to grow as Engine's connectivity surfaces expand.

You will operate as a senior leader working closely with executives and across Supply, Product, Engineering, Operations, and Partnerships. This is a builder's role: you will turn an ambitious vision for group travel into a clear strategy, a prioritized connectivity roadmap, and a set of signed, activated partnerships that expand what Engine can offer customers.

What You'll Do

• Own Engine's group connectivity strategy - defining how group bookings move across partners and platforms, and where we build first to unlock supply

• Set the strategy for deeper group connectivity, translating a north-star vision into a prioritized, buildable roadmap across the group booking lifecycle

• Lead the supply and connectivity partnerships that power group travel - with hotel chains, connectivity providers, technology platforms, and intermediaries - from first conversation through signed, activated agreements

• Contribute to Engine's broader connectivity strategy - bringing a partnerships and technical perspective to how supply connects across the platform, in close partnership with Supply and Lodging leadership

• Build relationships with connectivity providers and technology partners that support our group travel platform and Engine's wider supply surfaces

• Partner closely with Product and Engineering to shape group connectivity capabilities and integrations, informing the roadmap from a strategy and partnership lens

• Act as a subject-matter expert on the group travel landscape, connectivity models, and the technology that moves group bookings across the ecosystem

description:
We are seeking an experienced healthcare risk management and regulatory compliance leader to serve as Associate Vice President of Risk Management and Regulatory Compliance. This corporate leadership role provides oversight for company-wide risk management, patient safety, performance improvement, regulatory readiness, and licensure compliance activities across behavioral health facilities.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, detail-oriented leader with strong clinical, regulatory, and performance improvement knowledge and the ability to support facility leaders through audits, surveys, incident reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous readiness activities.
What You’ll Do

• Lead and maintain the company-wide risk management program, including the written risk management plan, related policies and procedures, and annual evaluation of program effectiveness.

• Demonstrated leadership, communication, collaboration, negotiation, research, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to analyze data, lead performance improvement teams, prepare reports and business correspondence, and present information effectively to leadership groups.

• Ability to work effectively with diverse populations and across multiple facilities.

Compensation, Benefits, and Location

• Job Type: Full-time, exempt leadership position.

This role may require standing, walking, sitting, reaching, speaking, hearing, using hands for computer or documentation tasks, and occasionally lifting or moving up to 50 pounds. title: AI Engineer- Applied AI
description:
Summary
About the Product
Concierge is Guidewire's omnichannel AI agent for P&C carriers. It answers the phone when a policyholder has just had an accident, takes first notice of loss, asks the questions a good adjuster would ask, and writes a clean claim into ClaimCenter. It runs in production today with real carriers and real policyholders, not as a demo.

Two things make this harder than a typical chatbot. First, it has synchronous voice: latency is a product requirement, not a metric on a dashboard. Second, FNOL is a regulated event where the quality of the intake determines the eventual cost of the claim. A missed question early is a bigger loss reserve later.
The Role:
You will build, evaluate, and harden the agent itself: the orchestration, the context it sees, the tools it can call, and the evals that tell us whether a change made it better or just different.

Our rollout philosophy is a dimmer, not a light switch. We widen the agent's autonomy one notch at a time, and every notch has to be earned with evidence. Much of your work is producing that evidence, then acting on what it says.
Job Description
What you'll do

• Own end-to-end slices of the agent: prompt and context architecture, retrieval over policy and coverage data, tool and API calls into core claims systems, and handoff to a human when the agent should stop.

• Build and run the eval loop, golden sets, trajectory evaluation, LLM-as-judge, error analysis on real production call traces, and make it the thing that gates releases.

• Drive containment and resolution rates up without trading away accuracy, and instrument the system well enough that we can tell which of the two moved.

• Work directly on the voice path: turn-taking, interruption, latency budgets, and the telephony layer underneath (LiveKit, SIP).

• Sit in on carrier calls and listen to recordings. The best fixes usually come from hearing where the conversation went sideways, not from reading the logs.

What we're looking for
1. Building and deploying AI applications. You've shipped an LLM application that real users depend on, and you know that the hard part is that the output is not predictable. You're fluent in the building blocks LLMs, context engineering, RAG, agentic workflows, and you have real ML and deep learning depth underneath that fluency. Most importantly, you know how to make an unpredictable system behave predictably enough to trust: disciplined evals, error analysis, and statistical measurement rather than vibes and a handful of spot checks.
2. Software engineering fundamentals. You can reason about cost, latency, reliability, and scalability as tradeoffs rather than goals, and you know which ones you're making. You've designed data stores and distributed systems, you write tests, and you take security and privacy seriously while advocating CI/CD process automation. We handle claims data, recorded calls, and PII under carrier and regulatory scrutiny.
3. Using coding agents. You work with coding agents daily and you're good at it: managing their context, deciding when a spec is worth writing and when it isn't, giving them verifiers so they can close their own loops, and knowing when to intervene versus leave them alone. You also keep changing how you work as the tooling changes, rather than settling into a 2025 workflow.
4. Shaping the build. You won't be handed a finished spec. You'll be in the room where we decide what the agent should do next, which means you need product sense and enough insurance context to argue about it. You'll know when to put an MVP in front of a carrier next week and when a claims workflow demands that we slow down and get it right the first time.
Underneath all four: you keep learning. This field looks different every six months and we expect to keep changing our minds.

• Insurance, claims, or another regulated domain where being wrong has a cost attached

title: Adversarial Simulation Lead
description:
Ardent is seeking an Adversarial Simulation Lead to join our team.
This is a remote position with expected travel to Tallahassee, FL.
Position Description:
Ardent is seeking a Adversarial Simulation Lead to plan and execute controlled, threat-informed simulations that test whether access controls, monitoring, and detection processes function together under realistic operating conditions. The role performs only explicitly authorized activities within agency-specific, Rules of Engagement and prioritizes safe execution, deconfliction, evidentiary rigor, and operational relevance across a potentially broad multi-agency environment.
Responsibilities and Duties:

• Translate approved control objectives into safe adversary-behavior simulations and test cases aligned to selected kill-chain stages and MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

• Develop agency-specific Rules of Engagement inputs covering authorized systems, windows, accounts, techniques, tools, prohibitions, notifications, deconfliction, stop-work conditions, evidence handling, and escalation.

• Execute approved access-control stress tests, privilege-boundary attempts, anomaly generation, endpoint/network activity, vulnerability validation, and related verification techniques.

• Coordinate closely with the Detection & Monitoring Analyst to trace events from activity initiation through telemetry, alerting, triage, escalation, and response.

• Minimize operational risk by confirming preconditions, rollback considerations, safety constraints, communications, and stop conditions before testing.

• Capture reproducible evidence, including command or tool context, screenshots, packet or event data, logs, timestamps, affected assets, observed outcomes, and analytic notes.

• Perform root-cause analysis and develop technically feasible hardening or detection-improvement recommendations, clearly separated from factual AUP reporting.

• Support retesting of approved remediated findings and document whether expected control performance is demonstrated.

• Contribute to workshops and reusable job aids explaining simulation design, evidence, and defensive lessons.

Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, digital forensics, information technology, computer science, or related field.

• Proof of relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISA, PMP, CEH, or other relevant certifications.

• 7 years in adversary simulation, penetration testing, threat hunting, digital forensics, incident response, vulnerability assessment, or security engineering.

• Demonstrated ability to conduct controlled testing in production-sensitive or regulated environments under formal authorization.

• Hands-on knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, identity and access control, endpoint and network telemetry, SIEM/EDR/XDR, vulnerability tools, cloud security, and evidence preservation.

• Ability to explain operational consequences and mitigation options to technical and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience leading purple-team exercises or adversary campaigns.

• Experience testing Zero Trust or identity-centric controls.

• Cloud, web application, API, Active Directory, firewall, and multi-tenant security operations experience.

• GIAC penetration testing or forensic certifications.

Due to the nature of the work we support, all candidates in consideration for this role must be willing to undergo the government issued background investigation process.

title: Healthcare Claims Supervisor
description:
Position: Healthcare Claims Supervisor
Location: Remote, Eastern Standard Time (EST) based in the Continental United States.
Reports To: Program Director

Overview:
J29 is an employee centered health and human service management consulting company that specializes in processing, reviewing, and analyzing claims, records, disputes, and audits. Established in 2017, J29 prides itself on its employee centric culture and high employee retention rates that allow us to ensure that we are creating a working environment that prioritizes employee experience. Our team brings corporate performance where we provide our clinical, healthcare policy, and compliance expertise through our support to health and human service programs.

J29 is seeking an experienced Healthcare Claims Supervisor to support the World Trade Center Health Program Third-Party Administrator contract. Reporting to the Program Director, this position will provide daily supervisory oversight and technical leadership for a growing healthcare claims processing team. The team is expected to begin with at least two direct reports and expand as program operations grow.

The Healthcare Claims Supervisor will be responsible for staff direction, claims quality, productivity, operational readiness, and consistent application of program requirements. The role requires strong knowledge of healthcare claims adjudication, coordination of benefits (COB), claims system workflows, and new program implementation. • Identify COB-related trends, errors, and training needs, and recommend procedural or system improvements.

title: Customer Experience Specialist
description:
The Customer Experience Specialist (CXS) serves as an internal liaison between the Customer, the Customer Experience Account Manager (CXAM), Service Operations and Billing. The role is directly responsible for order accuracy and progression.
Primary Responsibilities (Essential Functions):
• Order creation - Understand and fulfill all requirements for a “complete” order every time, following established Standard Work. This includes pricing in place, profiles that are active and will remain active until receipt at facility, supplies requested, labor required, transportation needs, and waste inventory.
• Order scheduling - Coordinate directly with operations to schedule required work, using systems in place (Preview, CORE, etc.), while understanding that direct communication is sometimes needed to make sure service is provided that meets or exceeds customer expectations.
• Order follow up - Follow order progression through service, receipt at end of service location, and monitor all pieces required to fully invoice every order once service is completed. • Proficiency in CRM Microsoft Office Suite.
• Willingness to travel up to 10%.

The Opportunity:
At Grafana Labs , we build observability tools that help users understand, respond to, and improve their systems - regardless of scale, complexity, or tech stack. We recently started a skunkworks initiative with a mission to bring observability to the rest of the business. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence.

You will design and ship the core backend architecture that powers ingestion, context storage, retrieval APIs, and agent-facing integrations. This is an early-stage role on a high-autonomy team, so you should be comfortable working through ambiguity, making pragmatic architectural decisions, and building systems that can evolve from internal dogfooding to production-grade SaaS. As the team matures, there’s a broad opportunity to expand or redefine this role based on impact and initiative.

• Build the core backend services: Design, implement, test, and operate the first services for context ingestion, context indexing, retrieval orchestration, API access, source configuration, and system administration.

• Create a scalable SaaS foundation: Help define and build the architecture for a multi-tenant service, including tenant isolation, usage tracking, quotas, audit logs, background jobs, and reliable service boundaries.

title: Staff SW Systems Engineer 10531 – DPDK/VPP Data Plane Developer (SD-WAN Security)
Compiler Engineer – MLIR / PyTorch Infrastructure
description:
About us

Mythic is building the future of AI computing with breakthrough analog technology that delivers 100× the performance of traditional digital systems at the same power and cost. This unlocks bigger, more capable models and faster, more responsive applications-whether in edge devices like drones, robotics, and sensors, or in cloud and data center environments. Our technology powers everything from large language models and CNNs to advanced signal processing, and is engineered to operate from -40 °C to +125 °C, making it ideal for industrial, automotive, aerospace, and defense.
We’ve raised over $100M from world-class investors including Softbank, Threshold Ventures, Lux Capital, and DCVC, and secured multi-million-dollar customer contracts across multiple markets.
About the role
Join us in advancing the MLIR ecosystem at Mythic . You’ll help extend our existing high-level dialects and design a new hardware-aware low-level dialect, building conversion paths that bridge to our current IRs. Working closely with hardware engineers and ML developers, your work will expand interoperability with PyTorch and other frameworks, laying the groundwork for long-term innovation. The result: an MLIR-based stack that unifies hardware constraints with developer needs and accelerates adoption of modern ecosystems.
Here's what you will do

• Architect the migration of the existing compiler flow into MLIR, defining dialects, passes, and lowering strategies.

• Build conversion paths between MLIR and Mythic ’s custom low-level IR to keep both flows operational during migration.

• Define validation infrastructure within MLIR, including interpretation or execution paths for simulation and debugging.

• Enable compilation by extending MLIR integration across analog accelerators and digital subsystems.

• Leverage Torch-MLIR where PyTorch inputs are available, and guide future integration with PyTorch 2.0 compiler technologies (TorchInductor, TorchDynamo, Torch-MLIR)

Here's the background we hope you will have

• 3+ years of experience in compiler or high-performance systems development.

• Proficiency in modern C++ (C++14/17/20) and Python.

• Direct, hands-on experience with MLIR, including dialect design, compiler passes, or lowering pipelines.

• Strong understanding of compiler IRs and transformations, with the ability to reason about lowering from high-level ops to hardware-aware representations.

The following would be nice to have, but is not required

• Experience architecting complete MLIR flows: from frontend dialects down to hardware-aware dialects, including conversion to and from existing IRs.

• Familiarity with PyTorch compiler technologies, especially Torch-MLIR and integration paths with PyTorch 2.0 (TorchDynamo, TorchInductor).

• Knowledge of dataflow architectures, scheduling, and memory orchestration.

• Background in heterogeneous or specialized accelerators (e.g., analog compute, NPUs, GPUs, DSPs).

What we offer

• Shape the MLIR and PyTorch integration strategy for novel AI hardware.

• Opportunity to contribute upstream and influence the broader ML compiler ecosystem.

• Collaborate with a team spanning hardware, runtime, and compiler design.

• Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

At Mythic , we foster a collaborative and respectful environment where people can do their best work. We hire smart, capable individuals, provide the tools and support they need, and trust them to deliver. Our team brings a wide range of experiences and perspectives, which we see as a strength in solving hard problems together. We value professionalism, creativity, and integrity, and strive to make Mythic a place where every employee feels they belong and can contribute meaningfully.

We are seeking an analytical and action-oriented Real Estate Transactions Manager to be the “engine room” of our infrastructure acquisition team. In this role, you will take identified sites and drive them from initial interest to a signed lease or purchase agreement. title: Staff Accountant, Corporate Accounting & Consolidations - Full Time, Days
description:
Be a part of a world-class academic healthcare system at UChicago Medicine as a Staff Accountant. This position will be primarily a work-from-home opportunity, with the requirement to come onsite as needed.
The Staff Accountant, Corporate Accounting & Consolidations, is responsible for supporting the accurate and timely preparation of accounting records and financial reporting activities for the University of Chicago Health System and its related entities and partnerships. The Staff Accountant supports the monthly close process through the preparation of routine journal entries, account reconciliations, and financial schedules related to investments, debt, insurance, eliminations, and joint venture activities.
The Staff Accountant assists with quarterly and annual financial reporting, audit support, and other Corporate Accounting activities. The role works closely with members of Corporate Accounting, Treasury, and other departments to obtain information, resolve routine accounting questions, and ensure transactions are recorded accurately and in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
The position is expected to perform established accounting processes with increasing independence while escalating complex or non-routine accounting matters to senior team members. The role requires strong attention to detail, organization, and the ability to manage multiple deadlines in a collaborative environment.
Essential Job Functions

• Prepare routine monthly journal entries and supporting documentation for assigned accounting areas, which may include:

• Investment transactions, including income accruals, amortization, accretion, valuation adjustments, and gains/losses.

• Insurance prepaid and accrual activity.

• Entity eliminations and intercompany activity.

• Joint venture and partnership activity, including recording financial information provided by external partners.

• Bonds and debt service, including interest accruals, debt issuance cost amortization, and debt service payments.

• Grants and pledges, including recording, reconciling, and reporting related activity.

• Perform established accounting processes in accordance with GAAP and department procedures.

• Participate in the monthly close process by completing assigned tasks accurately and within established deadlines.

• Research and resolve accounting discrepancies, escalating complex or unusual items to senior team members.

• Prepare monthly account reconciliations for assigned investment, insurance, elimination, joint venture, debt, grants, pledges, and related accounts.

• Analyze account activity and investigate variances and reconciling items.

• Maintain accurate and organized supporting documentation for journal entries and reconciliations.

• Assist with roll-forward schedules and other supporting schedules used in financial reporting and audit activities.

• Follow up with internal departments and external parties as needed to obtain supporting information.

• Assist with the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting schedules.

• Support the preparation of bond and debt compliance reports by providing assigned financial information and supporting schedules.

• Assist with quarterly and annual financial statement close and reporting activities.

• Provide requested schedules, documentation, and account support for interim and year-end financial statement audits.

• Assist with maintaining audit schedules and responding to routine audit requests.

• Support the preparation of consolidated financial reporting by completing assigned accounting and reconciliation activities.

• Participate in special projects and operational improvement initiatives as requested by leadership.

• Assist with documenting accounting processes and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and accuracy.

• Support other members of the Corporate Accounting team with routine accounting and reporting activities as needed.

title: Senior Safety Management System (SMS) Analytics Specialist

description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver-The World's Most Experienced Driver™-to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Waymo Safety team works to promote and help to continuously improve the safety of Waymo’s fully autonomous driving technology. Our experts develop safety goals and strategies, and conduct safety engineering analyses to ensure safety is being considered throughout the design and development of our vehicles. The team develops and promotes safety strategies and policies for autonomous vehicles for its work with regulatory authorities, lawmakers, law enforcement and public and non-profit organizations. Our Safety Team also helps advise on compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety regulations.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule and reports to the Safety Management System Lead.

In the Senior Safety Management System (SMS) Analytics Specialist role, you will lead how Waymo measures and reports on the performance of its Safety Management System. This role sits at the intersection of data analytics and executive governance: you will develop and synthesize reliable metrics across our safety processes, increase awareness and understanding of SMS performance data, and translate complex trends into recommendations for senior leaders. When metrics highlight areas for improvement, you will partner across teams to ensure owners are assigned and solutions deliver measurable results. In this role, your work will directly drive continual improvement across Waymo’s safety programs.

You will:

• Develop Reliable Safety Performance Indicators: Design and refine SMS implementation, maturity, and effectiveness metrics grounded in industry best practices and international safety standards, assessing and maintaining metric quality and advising teams and leaders on proper metric interpretation and use.

• Map & Synthesize Multi-Domain Safety Management Metrics: Collect, quality-assure, and synthesize quantitative and qualitative metrics across multiple business functions and trace them to the company’s top-line safety objectives.

• Run SMS Performance Reporting Governance: Lead the processes and analytics workflows used to support executive leadership review of SMS performance data and aggregated trend analyses.

• Translate Signals into Executive Decision Material: Partner with data science, operational, and safety teams across Waymo to distill complex multi-source data into clear, decision-oriented briefings, dashboards, and continual-improvement recommendations for senior leaders.

• Drive Closed-Loop Action & Effectiveness Tracking: Monitor safety performance indicators against targets and thresholds; where indicators show adverse trends or fall short of targets, confirm an accountable owner is assigned and track action items through to verified closure and confirmed effectiveness.

• Scale Analytics Tooling & Audit Readiness: Define requirements for data collection, visualization, and reporting tools that improve the reliability and scalability of SMS performance measurement, and support preparation for domestic and international regulatory audits and evaluations.

title: CAAS Staff Accountant
description:
We are currently seeking a talented Staff Accountant to join our Client Accounting and Advisory Services department.
Boulay offers accounting and consulting services, integrating business and owner strategies that help clients understand their impact on future success. Our advice comes from a strong focus on serving privately held owner-managed organizations, from start-ups to established small and mid-size businesses. Our team specializes in helping to improve day-to-day operations by offering outsourced accounting services, including bookkeeping, controller, and CFO services.
The CAAS Staff Accountant is responsible for assisting our clients with their internal accounting needs by performing and reviewing a variety of diversified accounting tasks. This includes working with multiple clients to help process their accounts payable, accounts receivable, processing or assisting to process payroll under the review of the engagement leader and owner. Tasks may include working primarily independently at times and assisting the client with questions that arise day to day with the accounting department. This position also involves working cross-departmentally with other Boulay departments to effectively accomplish projects and tasks.
Client-Facing and Technical Work:

• Manage the daily transaction accounting activities, including but not limited to:

• Daily Sales, bank, and other account reconciliations

• Inventory management

• Accrual management

• Prepaid management

• Equity accounting management

• Accounts receivables and accounts payable management

• Management of critical client deadlines

• Payroll process and preparation

• Expense reimbursements

• Discuss and explain transactions/processes with clients in a group or one-on-one setting as needed

• Identify and recognize potential risks, concerns, or issues regarding the client file

• Maintain accounting records through data entry and file management

• Prepare complex sales and use tax returns

• Ensure compliance and adherence to relevant reporting requirements

• Maintain a chart of accounts

• Monitor and maintain fixed assets

• Prepare and review 1099 filings

• Prepare or assist to prepare financial statements

• Identify issues and communicate status updates with appropriate team member or Partner as necessary

• Maintain professional and appropriate conduct; represent Firm and self well in all work-related situations

• Follow all regulations and ethical standards set forth by the Firm and other governing bodies

• Develop an understanding of the client’s business practices

Requirements

• Associates Degree in Accounting

• 2+ years of related experience

• Strong computer skills and proficiency in various accounting and other software, including Microsoft Office Suite

• Strong knowledge of all areas of the general ledger, along with reconciliations and month-end / year-end close procedures

• Knowledge of GAAP

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills along with the ability to drive client and team meetings

• Ability to creatively solve problems and analyze client data

Preferred:

• Bachelor's Degree in Accounting

• Experience with QuickBooks (desktop or online) and/or other general ledger software
